{
  "findings": [
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/incidents/grouptype.py",
      "line": 11,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "MetricAlertDetectorHandler is abstract but registered as a detector handler",
      "body": "MetricAlertDetectorHandler subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler but does not implement the abstract members counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and build_occurrence_and_event_data. MetricAlertFire.detector_handler points to this class, and Detector.detector_handler instantiates group_type.detector_handler(detector). Any attempt to get the handler for a metric_alert_fire detector will raise TypeError instead of evaluating or safely no-oping. Either implement the required methods, provide safe stubs, or do not register this handler until it is concrete."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py",
      "line": 222,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "get_state_data raises KeyError when counter_names is empty",
      "body": "In StatefulDetectorHandler.get_state_data, counter_updates is initialized to {} and only populated if self.counter_names is truthy. Later DetectorStateData is constructed with counter_updates[gk] for every group key. If a subclass legitimately has counter_names == [], this raises KeyError for the first group key, making such a stateful detector unusable. Use a default mapping such as counter_updates.get(gk, {}) or always populate defaults for every requested group key."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py",
      "line": 265,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Dedupe marker is advanced before validating condition group",
      "body": "evaluate_group_key_value calls enqueue_dedupe_update(group_key, dedupe_value) before checking self.condition_group. process_detectors later calls commit_state_updates even when evaluate returns no results, so a packet that was skipped because the detector has no condition group still persists the new dedupe value. If the missing condition group is temporary or corrected later, that packet will never be re-evaluated, potentially losing alert transitions. The dedupe update should probably only be committed after the packet has actually been evaluated, or at least not when skipping for invalid configuration."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py",
      "line": 68,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Occurrences are emitted before state updates are committed",
      "body": "process_detectors calls create_issue_occurrence_from_result for every result and only afterwards calls handler.commit_state_updates(). If producing one of the occurrences or the subsequent state commit fails, the dedupe/state changes are not persisted. On retry the same packet will be evaluated again, and any occurrences already produced before the failure can be emitted again. Since this PR makes detector handlers produce real IssueOccurrence/StatusChangeMessage payloads, this path can create duplicate issues unless occurrence identifiers are guaranteed idempotent."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py",
      "line": 159,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "api",
      "title": "get_group_key_values type annotation excludes supported None group key",
      "body": "StatefulDetectorHandler.get_group_key_values is annotated as returning dict[str, int], but DetectorGroupKey is used throughout as an optional key and the tests pass {None: ...}. The abstract signature should be dict[DetectorGroupKey, int], or otherwise document None as a valid key, so subclasses and type checkers match the runtime behavior."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py",
      "line": 230,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "doc_defect",
      "title": "evaluate docstring still says it returns a list",
      "body": "StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate's docstring says it returns a list of DetectorEvaluationResult, but the method now returns a dict keyed by DetectorGroupKey. This can mislead implementers about the contract introduced by this PR."
    },
    {
      "file": "tests/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/test_detector.py",
      "line": 537,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "test_gap",
      "title": "Expected occurrence is built for the wrong group key",
      "body": "In TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe, the test evaluates evaluate_group_key_value with group_key 'group_key', but the expected occurrence is built with build_mock_occurrence_and_event(handler, 'val1', ...), giving it a fingerprint for 'val1'. If IssueOccurrence equality includes fingerprint, this test will fail; if equality ignores fingerprint, the test does not verify that the produced occurrence corresponds to the evaluated group key. The expected occurrence should be built with the same group_key being evaluated."
    }

findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is abstract but registered as a detector handler
findings.body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler but does not implement the abstract members counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and build_occurrence_and_event_data. MetricAlertFire.detector_handler points to this class, and Detector.detector_handler instantiates group_type.detector_handler(detector). Any attempt to get the handler for a metric_alert_fire detector will raise TypeError instead of evaluating or safely no-oping. Either implement the required methods, provide safe stubs, or do not register this handler until it is concrete.

findings.title: get_state_data raises KeyError when counter_names is empty
findings.body: In StatefulDetectorHandler.get_state_data, counter_updates is initialized to {} and only populated if self.counter_names is truthy. Later DetectorStateData is constructed with counter_updates[gk] for every group key. If a subclass legitimately has counter_names == [], this raises KeyError for the first group key, making such a stateful detector unusable. Use a default mapping such as counter_updates.get(gk, {}) or always populate defaults for every requested group key.

findings.title: Dedupe marker is advanced before validating condition group
findings.body: evaluate_group_key_value calls enqueue_dedupe_update(group_key, dedupe_value) before checking self.condition_group. process_detectors later calls commit_state_updates even when evaluate returns no results, so a packet that was skipped because the detector has no condition group still persists the new dedupe value. If the missing condition group is temporary or corrected later, that packet will never be re-evaluated, potentially losing alert transitions. The dedupe update should probably only be committed after the packet has actually been evaluated, or at least not when skipping for invalid configuration.

findings.title: Occurrences are emitted before state updates are committed
findings.body: process_detectors calls create_issue_occurrence_from_result for every result and only afterwards calls handler.commit_state_updates(). If producing one of the occurrences or the subsequent state commit fails, the dedupe/state changes are not persisted. On retry the same packet will be evaluated again, and any occurrences already produced before the failure can be emitted again. Since this PR makes detector handlers produce real IssueOccurrence/StatusChangeMessage payloads, this path can create duplicate issues unless occurrence identifiers are guaranteed idempotent.

findings.title: get_group_key_values type annotation excludes supported None group key
findings.body: StatefulDetectorHandler.get_group_key_values is annotated as returning dict[str, int], but DetectorGroupKey is used throughout as an optional key and the tests pass {None: ...}. The abstract signature should be dict[DetectorGroupKey, int], or otherwise document None as a valid key, so subclasses and type checkers match the runtime behavior.

findings.title: evaluate docstring still says it returns a list
findings.body: StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate's docstring says it returns a list of DetectorEvaluationResult, but the method now returns a dict keyed by DetectorGroupKey. This can mislead implementers about the contract introduced by this PR.

findings.title: Expected occurrence is built for the wrong group key
findings.body: In TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe, the test evaluates evaluate_group_key_value with group_key 'group_key', but the expected occurrence is built with build_mock_occurrence_and_event(handler, 'val1', ...), giving it a fingerprint for 'val1'. If IssueOccurrence equality includes fingerprint, this test will fail; if equality ignores fingerprint, the test does not verify that the produced occurrence corresponds to the evaluated group key. The expected occurrence should be built with the same group_key being evaluated.
